question: Should ambiguous outbound delivery entries with no reconciliation-capable adapter remain pending without consuming retry budget, or should they continue to terminalize as failed?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: pending deferral preserves future recoverability, while terminal failure bounds operator state and avoids indefinite ambiguous queue rows; code review cannot choose that product policy safely.

options.title: Accept pending deferral
options.body: Merge this mitigation after exact-head CI if maintainers prefer future reconciliation over terminalizing ambiguous no-adapter entries.

options.title: Require a bounded operator path
options.body: Ask for a cap, surfaced state, or cleanup/doctor path before merge if indefinite pending entries are not acceptable.

options.title: Defer to the broader ledger
options.body: Pause this PR and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87544 decide ambiguous delivery recovery semantics in one durable design.

recommendation.title: Accept pending deferral
recommendation.body: Merge this mitigation after exact-head CI if maintainers prefer future reconciliation over terminalizing ambiguous no-adapter entries.
